highlights.title: Wikipedia Workers Unionize for the First Time
highlights.summary: More than 200 people in roles such as engineering, finance, and communications will now be represented by the Communications Workers of America.
body: More than 200 staffers at the Wikimedia Foundation, the nonprofit behind the encyclopedia Wikipedia, have voted 158-14 to join the Communications Workers of America labor union. The US National Labor Relations Board counted ballots on Thursday.

Three Wikimedia employees tell WIRED they will now have a mechanism to challenge management as the organization faces growing competition from AI chatbots and a drop in volunteer editors. The 25-year-old, San Francisco-based foundation employs nearly 700 people across 39 countries, most of them working remotely. The contingent joining the union includes employees in functions such as software engineering, finance, communications.

Lauren de Lench, who has been a lead technical program manager at the Wikimedia Foundation since 2021, says she voted to unionize because she had seen too many colleagues decline to speak up during internal meetings out of fear of retaliation for raising issues or proposing far-out ideas.
“I want us to be loud and debate freely up and down the organizational chart because that’s how we move quickly, address challenges, and come up with the best collective solutions,” de Lench says.

highlights.title: Nobody Is Saying Why OpenAI and Anthropic Had Outages Today
highlights.summary: ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok all suffered outages at nearly the exact same time for reasons that remain murky.
body: Frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI all experienced rare outages on Thursday morning, creating downtime for their corresponding AI chatbots. SpaceX, xAI’s parent company, said on Thursday afternoon that the issues with Grok resulted from “an outage at our Memphis compute center this morning.”

The issues initially appeared to be linked because they coincided—perhaps the result of a shared third-party service provider—but neither OpenAI nor Anthropic cited an external source in comments to WIRED on Thursday. SpaceX, xAI’s parent company, did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment. But the company said as part of its public comments on Thursday: “We’d also like to apologize to our impacted compute partners.” Anthropic and xAI announced a “compute partnership” with SpaceX in May.

OpenAI spokesperson Kathleen Chaykowski tells WIRED: “A routing error starting around 7:43 am PT on Thursday, September 3, made ChatGPT and Codex unavailable for some users across platforms. As of about 8:17 am PT on Thursday, a solution was successfully implemented and is continuing to be monitored.”

highlights.title: The unusually muted Tesla Cybercab launch
highlights.summary: At a private, closed-door event in Austin, Texas today, Tesla officially launched its gilded car of the future. It's a huge milestone for Elon Musk, who has been hyping the imminent arrival of driverless cars for years and has bet the future of his company on AI, autonomous vehicles, and humanoid…
body: Tesla has 45 Cybercabs registered in Texas, though it’s unclear how many of them will be doing passenger trips.

It was an unusually muted event: with no livestream, pro-Tesla accounts on X.com were left streaming the webpage that tracks the number of Tesla robotaxis in Texas. Like last year’s robotaxi launch, the invite list was mostly pro-Tesla influencers, so as to blunt any possible criticism of its new products. Invitee Chuck Cook said the company had him sign an NDA and agreed to an embargo requiring to wait to post content until after the event was over. On X, pro-Tesla accounts who weren’t invited grumbled aboutthe decision; Not a Tesla App accused the company of “dropping the ball.”

With the new Cybercabs, Tesla now has 256 unsupervised autonomous vehicles in operation across six cities, according to Robotaxi Tracker. By comparison, Alphabet’s Waymo is currently operating approximately 4,000 vehicles across 14 cities.

body: Data center developer Crusoe, which counts Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI as its customers, has raised a new $3 billion round at a $30 billion valuation, Bloomberg reported.

The deal is being co-led by Atreides Management and Valor Equity Partners, and includes participation from Mubadala Capital, the asset management subsidiary of Abu Dhabi’s sovereign wealth fund Mubadala.
The company recently signed a massive $13 billion, five-year cloud contract to supply quantitative trading firm Jane Street with GPUs and AI infrastructure, Bloomberg reported.
The fresh fundraise comes 10 months after Crusoe raised a $1.38 billion round at a $10 billion valuation last October.

highlights.summary: Robert Greene's latest hybrid feature mixes documentary and fiction to focus on a pair of 40-something friends from Missouri, exposing hardships they face as ex-cons and fathers.
body: Director and editor Robert Greene continues to intriguingly blur the lines between fact, fiction and filmmaking in his new hybrid feature, Too Much Sugar, which premiered in Venice ’s Orizzonti sidebar.

The two eventually became friends, and then collaborators, with Greene deciding to make a feature about Holliger, his sizable family and his best friend and fellow carpenter, Michael Midgyett, aka “AccRite.” You can see what the director found appealing about such a character: Raised by a single mom, the former convict spent four years in jail before becoming a manual laborer and amateur boxer. He now dedicates his life to being the best father possible — no easy task when taking into account that he has six children from five different mothers.

Per his own words, Holliger excels at “making bad decisions that turn into great kids,” and such energy and positivity seem to rub off on his many offspring, who range from ages 8 to 24 and whom Holliger coaches through various sports (basketball, baseball, boxing and soccer) while also housing and feeding most of them with the help of his current partner, Amanda.

highlights.title: GPT-6 Astra Is Here—and OpenAI Thinks It May Kick Off the AGI Era
highlights.summary: OpenAI leaders think the company’s next generation model, which excels at computer use and coding, may mark a major milestone in AI development.
body: OpenAI announced Thursday the launch of its next generation AI model, GPT-6 Astra, which the company claims is state of the art at navigating computers and web browsers, writing software, and solving difficult math problems.

In a press briefing with reporters, OpenAI executives made it clear that they feel very confident about the company’s latest AI model. President and cofounder Greg Brockman says he personally believes the world is now in the era of artificial general intelligence, or AI systems that are generally smarter than humans.

“It’s not unreasonable to feel that we are now in the AGI era,” Brockman told reporters. “I think that if we fast-forward a couple of years, when we look back and say, ‘When was it really that AGI was created?’ I think it's going to be about this time, and I think it might be about this model."

highlights.title: No Britons left in US Open singles as Dart & Jones lose
highlights.summary: Harriet Dart and Francesca Jones fall to seeded players as British interest in the US Open singles ends in the second round.
body: Harriet Dart and Francesca Jones both fell to seeded players as British interest in the US Open singles ended in the second round.
Dart said she felt "under the weather" during her 6-2 6-2 defeat by Czech 25th seed Marie Bouzkova as temperatures reached around 30C in New York.
Her loss meant Jones was the last Briton standing in either singles draw, and she acquitted herself well before falling 6-4 6-4 to 14th seed and rising American star Iva Jovic.
Nine British players competed in the US Open main draws - the most since 1981 - with four coming through qualifying.

highlights.title: Your home organization can actually look stylish. These 27 designer-approved solutions are proof
highlights.summary: If you feel like you’re drowning in stuff and can’t find anything you need, there’s a box (or basket) for that. 11 products our writers rely on to organize and declutter. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Look around your house and be honest: are you drowning in stuff? I know I am. Between a toddler, one on the way, two cats and a personal inability to throw out junk “just in case”, it’s rare I see the actual surface of my floor or countertops.

Without a home organization system that works for you, the sheer amount of objects you have accumulated throughout the years can quickly overrun your home. Many of us tend to put away stuff “for now”, only for our closets and cabinets to fill up, preventing us from seeing what we own. “If you can’t find something, it can feel easier to order another one than to spend 20 minutes searching,” Amy Berryhill, a professional organizer and owner of Spiffy Chicks, said.

The best way to make space for everything you need is to make intentional – and stylish! – choices about how you organize your home. “We like to think about organization as an extension of the design process, finding ways to give everyday items a designated home without sacrificing beauty,” said Audrey Scheck, an interior designer and founder of Audrey Scheck Design.

The ITIA consulted an independent scientific expert at a World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada)-accredited laboratory, who stated the explanation was consistent with the level of cocaine found in his sample.

highlights.summary: OpenAI's next big model is here: GPT-6 Astra. The company calls it a "generational leap in capability" for areas like cybersecurity, professional work, software engineering, science, and computer use.
body: It emphasized stronger guardrails for GPT-6 Astra after the company’s models hacked Hugging Face.

“If we fast-forward a couple of years, and we look back and say, ‘When was it, really, that AGI was created?’ I think it’s going to be about this time, and I think it might be about this model,” OpenAI president Greg Brockman said during a Thursday press briefing. Later in the call, he added, “For me personally, I do think we’re there … I think it’s not unreasonable to feel that we are now in the AGI era.”

The news comes more than a year after the release of GPT-5, and nearly two months after the release of GPT-5.6, the last iteration of the previous model suite. The model rolls out today to enterprise OpenAI’s cybersecurity customers (enterprise customers with access to its Daybreak platform). Over the next several days, OpenAI president Greg Brockman said, it will be released to all Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. It’ll also be available via the OpenAI API and AWS.

highlights.summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is still secretly counting two measles deaths that were deleted from the agency's public measles data—a deletion that occurred at the direct request of anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., according to two reports released today.
body: Early today, Reuters reported that Kennedy instructed new CDC director Erica Schwartz to delete the two deaths from the agency’s website. CDC staff had reportedly already reviewed information about the deaths and accepted the characterization that they were measles-related. Still, Schwartz deleted the deaths without objection, insiders told Reuters. According to previous reporting, the two deaths were added and then removed from the CDC’s website within hours on August 30.

The deaths were of a newborn and a child, and they were reported last week by health officials in Pennsylvania. The state’s ongoing measles outbreak has sickened 540 so far, including 119 just in the last week.

This afternoon, Inside Medicine reported that an internal CDC database still includes the two deaths, according to a screenshot that was reportedly verified by CDC staff. The database, called “One CDC Data Platform,” is accessible to state and local health officials as well as CDC employees.
Ars Technica reached out to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) about the discrepancy, but it did not immediately respond.

highlights.title: OpenAI Cut Off a Billion-Dollar Customer to Avoid Elon Musk
highlights.summary: OpenAI recently estimated its Cursor partnership would make more than $1 billion in revenue a year, WIRED has learned. It still walked away after Elon Musk’s SpaceX acquired the AI coding startup.
body: In a late-night blog post last Friday, OpenAI said it would wind down its partnership with Cursor, the startup behind one of the most popular AI coding tools on the market. The reason OpenAI gave for the decision is effectively that it can’t trust Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX recently acquired Cursor in a $60 billion deal.

In doing so, OpenAI walked away from one of its most important customers. Cursor has long paid OpenAI fees to offer the ChatGPT-maker’s models to developers using its AI coding editor. At the start of 2026, Cursor was one of OpenAI’s top five customers in terms of revenue, people familiar with the matter tell WIRED. By the spring of this year, OpenAI estimated Cursor would bring in more than $1 billion in annualized revenue for the ChatGPT maker, based on the partnership’s performance at that time, the people said.

The figures, which have not been previously reported, indicate the financial loss OpenAI is willing to take on to avoid doing business with Musk. OpenAI declined to comment. Representatives for SpaceX and Cursor did not immediately respond to WIRED's request for comment.

highlights.title: Gloria Steinem obituary
highlights.summary: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists. Gloria Steinem, who has died aged 92, was a writer, community organiser, political campaigner and a charismatic feminist activist who called herself “an entrepreneur of social change”.
body: Steinem, unlike some of her contemporaries, never recanted or modified her many causes, which included civil rights, violence against women, and the struggle for equality. She continued to argue that every economics course ought to start not with production but with reproduction, and an understanding of the patriarchal instinct to restrict a woman’s right to contraception and abortion.

She was one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken critics throughout his rise to power. She labelled him “harasser in chief”, a man whose rhetoric and conduct ran counter to the values she had dedicated her life to advocating.

In 1963, when Betty Friedan published The Feminine Mystique – describing the frustration of affluent, well-educated, middle-class white women trapped in domesticity – Steinem was “a girl reporter” living in New York, working on The Beach Book, a compendium of extracts from literature about beaches and tips on what to do in the sun. A rising media star who was later described, to her annoyance, as “the world’s most beautiful byline”, she had already begun to make connections: she asked the economist JK Galbraith to write the foreword, and he agreed.
points: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists.

highlights.title: Nvidia launches free tool that links idle computers into a personal AI data center
highlights.summary: Nvidia is announcing its new Personal AI Router (PAIR), a free tool that syncs up your home computers for tackling local AI inference tasks with tools like Ollama and LM Studio. Let's get the obvious thing out of the way, despite what its name might imply: PAIR is not a hardware router.
body: PAIR is designed to get your desktop and laptop working together on local AI tasks when not in use.

The key thing here is that PAIR uses your in-home systems when they’re idle to avoid interfering with other tasks. And this disaggregated system of computers can work in parallel to chew through lots of processing requests — which should be helpful for an agentic workflow that breaks complex tasks into smaller jobs. This should prevent large bottlenecks on a single GPU, and Nvidia says PAIR can adapt as devices join or leave the network — including if a user does something like start playing a game on their desktop PC.

Players can now stick with their original civilization throughout an entire campaign rather than being forced to switch civilizations at each Age transition, while new systems such as Syncretism and Affirmation give players more control over how their civilization develops.

highlights.title: My dad died suddenly with no will. Am I morally obliged to share his estate with my estranged half-sibling? | Leading questions
highlights.summary: It’s kind of you to wonder if you should change the way things were left, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But it’s possible his preference is already clear. My dad died suddenly earlier this year, with no will, and I am unsure as to how I should distribute the estate.
body: My dad was a very ethical person. While his death was unexpected, he had a sense it was coming. About six months before he died, he arranged for the disposal of many personal effects. The lack of a will, given his self-discipline and preferences for forward planning, is odd.

My dad has two daughters from a previous relationship, who he was not in contact with until I was in my mid-30s. Their mum had remarried after separating from our dad, and her new husband had formally adopted both her girls. My dad was delighted to resume contact with one half-sister. Another, two years younger, wanted nothing to do with him and firmly disapproved of her sister’s choice to re-establish contact.

Some 10 years ago, I started my own family, relocated to remove myself from domestic abuse, and joined the league of parents of children with additional needs. My dad mentioned that he had a little money put aside that could go towards legal costs, should courts ever become involved in arrangements for my son.
